metadata.title: Jordi Visser's "25 Names" — Vera Rubin Supply Chain Reconstruction
metadata.speaker: Reconstruction brief — compiled from public sources, not a single video

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 1 — Nvidia invested ~$2B (March 2026) + multibillion purchase commitment; silicon photonics already in Spectrum-X switches; ELS laser source for CPO; capacity doubling through CY27. — The single most-cited photonics supplier in every teardown; earnings step-up begins H2 2026 as Spectrum-6 CPO ramps.

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 2 — Mirror deal: ~$2B Nvidia investment + purchase commitment; primary external-laser-source (ELS) supplier with a ~15-month qualification lead; ~$480M Nvidia CPO revenue estimated FY27. — Highest near-term Nvidia CPO revenue share; new US fab capacity; the classic "step-up" profile.

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 3 — Thailand-based ODM assembling optical transceivers, CPO modules and laser modules; named by Nvidia in the CPO ecosystem; dominant contract manufacturer for US optics designers. — Assembly node where transceiver + CPO volumes convert to revenue; historically under-owned vs. designer peers.

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 4 — Optical systems & coherent DSPs; WaveLogic coherent optics for data-center interconnect; supplies hyperscaler network fabrics alongside Nvidia ecosystems. — Pure-play optical at the systems level; estimate revisions lag transceiver makers — a later "step-up" candidate.

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 5 — Acquired Infinera (2025) — coherent optics, plus silicon photonics push; large optical transport installed base inside telco/AI backbones. — Infinera integration + AI datacenter optics is a classic revision-up story; European name US funds under-weight.

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 6 — Owns Acacia (silicon photonics, coherent modules); ships 800G optics into AI fabrics; NVIDIA-named in optical ecosystem discussions. — Defensive optics incumbent; multiples and revisions offer room vs. the semiconductor complex.

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 7 — Optical DSPs (PAM4), Tomahawk/Jericho Ethernet switches, its own CPO program; ESUN alliance member with Nvidia, Marvell, AMD for scale-out optical standards. — Mixed CPO threat vs. pluggables, but the scale-out networking step-up is real; huge AI revenue base.

conviction_map.stance: WATCHING / HIGH-CONFIDENCE candidate (reconstructed, not independently confirmed)
conviction_map.core_thesis: 8 — PCIe Gen6 retimers (Aries 6), Scorpio switches, CXL memory controllers — signal-integrity silicon for the densest racks ever built (1,300+ chips/NVL72). — Content-per-rack rises with Vera Rubin complexity; guidance beats consensus; "step-up" already visible.

9 — World's largest optical transceiver maker; 800G/1.6T modules into hyperscalers; dominant in Nvidia-adjacent networks. — The archetypal "many Asian" name; transceiver step-up with pricing power — exactly his screen.
16 — Largest fiber producer globally; Nvidia-ecosystem partner; fiber demand driven by rack-scale networking. — Global fiber upturn + AI; China-listed/HK name with step-up in orders.
17 — Chinese fiber/cable giant; submarine + datacenter connectivity. — Volume fiber play on the same demand curve.

18 — Taiwanese fiber-optic component maker explicitly named by Nvidia in CPO ecosystem materials (fiber, micro-optics, connectors). — A direct Nvidia-named partner that US investors barely know — the report's exact profile.

20 — Hybrid photonics platform (passive+active integration); 800G/CPO roadmap; micro-cap with design-win optionality. — The speculative "step-up lottery ticket" — fits his small/mid-cap thematic skew.

21 — Pure-play InP/GaAs compound-semiconductor substrates — the raw material bottleneck behind every CPO laser (supplies Coherent/Lumentum/Ayar ecosystem). — ~$350M market cap, off most radars; the classic second-order scarcity name.
22 — Polymer photonics / electro-optic modulators; long-running story, commercial ramp still unproven. — Speculative next-gen photonics; only fits if the report reaches beyond proven suppliers.

23 — 800VDC power racks, liquid-cooled busbars, UPS — one of the primary rack-level power partners for the 800V architecture. — The 800 VDC half of his paper; Taiwan mega-cap, under-covered by US investors.

25 — "Gold standard" 48V-to-sub-1V last-inch conversion (per Infineon materials); qualified for Nvidia's next-gen platform H2 2025. — Qualification + Nvidia ramp = the earnings inflection his screen hunts for.

26 — 800VDC power racks + NVLink 6 system integration + full-rack assembly; appears across 3+ subsystems. — Broad Vera Rubin exposure beyond optics; contract-manufacturing margins improve with utilization.
